site.anchor: a honra da pessoa jurídica não está codificada

source.quote: Caluniar alguém

citations.cite: CP arts. 138, 139 e 140, caput — "alguém"

readings.description: "Alguém" is a natural person: a legal person has no honour in the Code's sense and cannot be the victim of calúnia, difamação or injúria.

citations.cite: CP arts. 138 a 140 — "alguém"; art. 138, § 2º extends calúnia to the dead, and nothing extends any of the three to legal persons

readings.description: A legal person can be the victim of difamação (it has a reputation), and of calúnia where the fact imputed is a crime a legal person can commit (the environmental crimes of Lei nº 9.605/1998, art. 3º); not of injúria, which protects dignity and decorum.

citations.cite: Lei nº 9.605/1998, art. 3º (responsabilidade penal da pessoa jurídica)

taken.rationale: NONE TAKEN: the fork is open. The schema asks for a reading here, and this is the one the Code's words lean to; the encoding does not apply it. Where the one offended is a legal person (`ofendido` is NOTHING), all three crime predicates return the named refusal `a honra da pessoa jurídica não está codificada`. No court decision was fetched, and the courts' answers are reported to differ by crime.

notes: Searched only the Code and Lei nº 9.605/1998's art. 3º by memory of it; no STF or STJ decision was fetched. The question is for a Brazilian criminal lawyer (notes/g2b.md § 7).

site.anchor: calúnia consumada (art. 138; art. 14, I)

source.quote: Caluniar alguém, imputando-lhe falsamente fato definido como crime

citations.cite: CP arts. 138 a 140, caput
CP art. 14, I — "consumado, quando nele se reúnem todos os elementos de sua definição legal"

readings.description: Calúnia and difamação attack reputation (honra objetiva) and are consummated when the imputation reaches someone other than the one offended; injúria attacks dignity (honra subjetiva) and is consummated when the offence reaches the one offended. Before that, an interrupted execution (an intercepted letter) is an attempt.

citations.cite: CP art. 139 — "ofensivo à sua reputação"; art. 140 — "ofendendo-lhe a dignidade ou o decoro"
CP art. 14, I e II

readings.description: Each is consummated as soon as the words are uttered or written, whoever learns of them.

citations.cite: CP arts. 138 a 140 — the verbs name the act, not its reception

readings.foreclosure: Reputation is what others think, and dignity what the offended feels: an imputation no third person learns of does not touch the first, and an insult the offended never learns of does not touch the second. The reading would also leave no room for the attempt the Code allows in written forms.

taken.rationale: The two are told apart by the good each protects, which the chapter's own words name (reputation; dignity or decorum). The facts are the circumstances `a ofensa chegou ao conhecimento de terceiro` and `a ofensa chegou ao conhecimento do ofendido`.

witnesses: cp-g2b-honra-testes.l4: `difamação só ao ofendido` (not difamação) and `injúria só a terceiro` (not injúria)

site.anchor: crime de difamação (art. 139)

source.quote_absent_reason: The question is not about words the Code prints: no article says which of two overlapping tipos prevails. It arises where the facts meet the words of two articles at once (a calúnia whose fact also offends reputation; a threat made in the context of art. 147-C).

readings.description: Each crime predicate reports whether the facts meet its own article's words; where two are met, both are reported, and the apparent conflict (speciality, consunção) is resolved by the judge.

citations.cite: CP arts. 138 a 140; 147 e 147-C — each defines its own tipo

readings.description: Build speciality into the predicates, so that only the more specific tipo is reported (difamação false wherever calúnia holds; ameaça false wherever art. 147-C holds).
readings.rejection_rationale: The principles that resolve an apparent conflict of norms are not written in the Code; coding one would pre-empt a judgement the court makes on the whole case, and would hide from the reader that the facts meet the other tipo's words too.

taken.rationale: Literal predicates, and the overlap stated in the comments at art. 147-C and in the notes.

witnesses: cp-g2b-constrangimento-ameaca-testes.l4: `ameaça da facção` meets both art. 147 and art. 147-C

Lei nº 13.964/2019, art. 20 — "Esta Lei entra em vigor após decorridos 30 (trinta) dias de sua publicação oficial"

citations.cite: Lei nº 13.964/2019, art. 20; promulgação das partes vetadas, DOU 30.4.2021 (Senado Notícias, 30.4.2021)

Vladimir Aras, 'Vigor de partes vetadas de lei cujos vetos foram rejeitados', ConJur, 10.10.2021, relying on STF RE 85.950/RS (1976): the vetoed part enters into force by the law's own vigência rule, counted from its own publication

readings.description: In force with the rest of Lei nº 13.964/2019, thirty days after its publication of 24.12.2019 (23.1.2020): Planalto's "(Vigência)" link beside § 2º points at art. 20.

citations.cite: CP art. 141, § 2º — Planalto's "(Vigência)" link to L13964.htm#art20

readings.rejection_rationale: A vetoed provision was not law until its promulgation; it cannot have been in force before it was published.

readings.description: In force on the day the promulgated parts were published, 30.4.2021, with no fresh vacatio.

citations.cite: Promulgação das partes vetadas da Lei nº 13.964/2019, DOU 30.4.2021

readings.foreclosure: The promulgated text is part of Lei nº 13.964/2019, whose art. 20 sets a vacatio; nothing in the promulgation dispenses with it. The one authority found (RE 85.950, via Aras) applies the law's own rule.

taken.rationale: The reading with an authority behind it. The vigência constant is 30.5.2021, and the gate is tested on that day and the day before.

witnesses: cp-g2b-honra-testes.l4: `injúria em rede social na véspera` (29.5.2021: no § 2º here; under naDataDaPromulgacao it would apply)

CP art. 150, § 1º — "com o emprego de violência ou de arma"

STJ Súmula 174 (toy gun) — cancelled, REsp 213.054/SP, 3ª Seção, 24.10.2002

citations.cite: CP art. 146, § 1º — "armas"

readings.foreclosure: Where the Code wants a narrower class it names it ("arma de fogo", "arma branca"); the danger the increase answers is the same with an improvised weapon.

citations.cite: CP art. 146, § 1º

site.anchor: a ação penal da injúria real com lesão corporal leve não está codificada

source.quote: salvo quando, no caso do art. 140, § 2º, da violência resulta lesão corporal.

citations.cite: CP art. 145, caput
Lei nº 9.099/1995, art. 88 (as quoted in M-sweep-b-16)

readings.description: The exception removes the private action and the Code states no other, so art. 100's default governs: public and unconditional, whatever the injury.

citations.cite: CP art. 145, caput; art. 100

readings.description: Where the injury is slight, Lei nº 9.099/1995, art. 88 makes the action conditional on representação, by analogy with the crime of lesão corporal leve; unconditional for serious injury or death.

citations.cite: Lei nº 9.099/1995, art. 88 — "dependerá de representação a ação penal relativa aos crimes de lesões corporais leves e lesões culposas"

taken.rationale: NONE TAKEN for a slight injury: `a ação penal do art. 145` refuses there. For serious injury or death both readings agree (public and unconditional), and that is what the rule returns. The schema asks for a reading; this one is named only because it is the one both readings share beyond slight injury.

witnesses: cp-g2b-honra-testes.l4: `injúria real com lesão leve` (refused) against `injúria real com lesão grave` (public and unconditional)
notes: F-sweep-b-07 (g2a's, on art. 129) is the neighbouring question; its settlement may settle this one.

citations.cite: CP art. 141, II

readings.foreclosure: The second limb repeats "contra" and names the offices, which would be idle if they were only an instance of the first limb; Lei nº 14.197/2021 added them to protect the institutions' heads as such.

site.anchor: as causas do art. 141 alcançam também a multa

source.quote: As penas aplicam-se cumulativamente e em dobro

citations.cite: CP art. 146, § 1º
CP art. 141, caput — "As penas cominadas neste Capítulo aumentam-se de um terço"

readings.description: Where the words name "as penas" (plural) — and art. 146, § 1º names them in the same breath as making the fine cumulative — the increase reaches the fine as well: the judge applies the same fraction to the number of dias-multa.

citations.cite: CP art. 146, § 1º; art. 141, caput

readings.description: A cause scales the custodial range only; the number of dias-multa is fixed under arts. 49 and 60 (the reading of the shared machinery, F-g0-28).

citations.cite: CP art. 58; art. 60

readings.foreclosure: The machinery's reading is about what `Pena cominada` can carry, and g0 left the question, for words that name the fine, to this article's encoder; these words do name it.

taken.rationale: Stated, not computed, because `Pena cominada` carries no number of day-fines: the constants `as causas do art. 141 alcançam também a multa` and `o dobro do art. 146, § 1º, alcança também a multa` are TRUE, and the custodial range is scaled by the shared machinery.

notes: g0's side of the same question is F-g0-28 (cp-pena's machinery); the two do not conflict: F-g0-28 takes the machinery's reading for the shared arithmetic and hands articles whose words reach the fine to their encoders.

site.anchor: as opções do juiz pelo art. 140, § 1º

source.quote: § 1º - O juiz pode deixar de aplicar a pena:

citations.cite: CP art. 140, § 1º, I e II

readings.description: The judge's power reaches every form of injúria, §§ 2º and 3º included: the incisos speak of "a injúria", and a power in the accused's favour is not narrowed by placement.

citations.cite: CP art. 140, § 1º, I — "provocou diretamente a injúria"; II — "retorsão imediata, que consista em outra injúria"

readings.description: The power stands before §§ 2º and 3º and reaches the simple injúria only (the reading STJ Tema 1087 gave art. 155, § 1º).

citations.cite: CP art. 140 — the order of §§ 1º to 3º

readings.foreclosure: Tema 1087 narrowed an increase, where the placement argument favours the accused; applied here it would narrow a benefit, which is the opposite use.

site.anchor: crime de perseguição (art. 147-A)

source.quote: Perseguir alguém, reiteradamente e por qualquer meio

citations.cite: CP art. 147-A — "reiteradamente"
CP art. 146-A — "Intimidar sistematicamente", "de modo intencional e repetitivo"

readings.description: Both are habitual crimes: the repetition is an element, and a single act is either part of the habit (not yet the crime) or the habit is complete (the crime). There is no attempt.

citations.cite: CP arts. 146-A e 147-A

readings.description: An attempt is possible where the course of conduct was begun with the required intent and stopped from outside.

citations.cite: CP art. 14, II

readings.foreclosure: Each act of the course is lawful or another crime on its own; making the first act of a habit an attempt would punish a single act the article does not reach.

taken.rationale: No attempt predicate for arts. 146-A and 147-A; the crime predicates require the repetition.

site.anchor: a entrada é a do art. 22 da Lei nº 13.869, de 2019

Lei 13.869/2019 art. 22 caput, § 1º III, § 2º

readings.description: A public agent acting as such is punished under Lei 13.869 art. 22, which is special and later. The same law revoked art. 150 § 2º, which had covered officials. For warrant execution, 'dia' is the window 5h–21h (art. 22 § 1º III). For private persons 'noite' remains a judgement input.

citations.cite: Lei 13.869/2019 art. 22 caput, § 1º III, § 2º

readings.description: Art. 150 applies to everyone. Lei 13.869 adds a crime for authorities without displacing art. 150. 'Dia/noite' are natural daylight and darkness for every purpose.

citations.cite: CP art. 150 caput, § 1º, § 3º I

readings.foreclosure: Lei nº 13.869/2019 both created the special crime and revoked the paragraph of art. 150 that had governed officials, which shows the legislator moving officials' entries out of art. 150.

taken.rationale: From 3.1.2020 (Lei nº 13.869/2019's vigência) `crime de violação de domicílio (art. 150)` is FALSE where the agent is a public official (art. 327's facts) acting in or on the pretext of the function; before that date art. 150 applies and the revoked § 2º refuses in the causes. 'durante a noite' is the judge's finding; its herald does not import the 21h–5h window.

site.anchor: não constitui crime (art. 150, § 3º)

source.quote: II - a qualquer hora do dia ou da noite, quando algum crime está sendo ali praticado ou na iminência de o ser.

citations.cite: CP art. 150, § 3º, II

readings.description: Entry is lawful when, beforehand, founded reasons (justified afterwards) indicated flagrante delito inside. This follows STF Tema 280 for entries by agents and Lei 13.869 art. 22 § 2º ('fundados indícios').

citations.cite: STF Tema 280 (RE 603.616)

readings.description: The exclusion requires that a crime in fact was being committed or was imminent, as the text says.

citations.cite: CP art. 150 § 3º II

readings.foreclosure: For a public agent, Tema 280 measures the lawfulness of the entry by the founded reasons available beforehand; the text's reading survives for everyone else, in the reading taken.

readings.description: Split by the agent's status, as the sweep's note allows: for a public agent acting as such, founded reasons of flagrante delito, justified afterwards, are enough; for anyone else, a crime must in fact have been under way or imminent.

citations.cite: STF Tema 280 (RE 603.616) — a thesis on entries by agents and authorities
CP art. 150 § 3º II — the text, for private persons

taken.rationale: Tema 280 is a constitutional thesis on CF art. 5º XI about agents and authorities; carrying it to a private person's entry would widen a criminal exclusion on a thesis that does not speak of them. `não constitui crime (art. 150, § 3º)` applies the founded-reasons limb only where `o agente é agente público agindo nessa qualidade`.

site.anchor: quer por um dos modos do art. 149, caput

source.quote: Reduzir alguém a condição análoga à de escravo, quer submetendo-o a trabalhos forçados ou a jornada exaustiva, quer sujeitando-o a condições degradantes de trabalho, quer restringindo, por qualquer meio, sua locomoção em razão de dívida contraída com o empregador ou preposto:

citations.cite: CP art. 149, caput (redação da Lei nº 10.803/2003)

readings.description: The modes are alternatives: forced labour, an exhausting working day, degrading conditions, or restriction of movement for debt. Restraint of movement is not required, but the violation must be intense and persistent.

citations.cite: STF Inq 3412, Tribunal Pleno, julgado em 29/03/2012 (via TST-RR-450-57.2017.5.23.0041)

readings.description: 'Condição análoga à de escravo' requires deprivation of liberty in every mode.

citations.cite: Rejected by STF Inq 3412

readings.rejection_rationale: Struck by STF Inq 3412: "não é necessário que se prove a coação física da liberdade de ir e vir ou mesmo o cerceamento da liberdade de locomoção".

taken.rationale: `quer por um dos modos do art. 149, caput` is a disjunction of the four modes, and the caput also needs the judge's finding `violação intensa e persistente, a juízo do juiz`.

site.anchor: a injúria é a da Lei nº 7.716, de 1989, art. 2º-A

source.quote: Injuriar alguém, ofendendo-lhe a dignidade ou o decoro:

citations.cite: CP art. 140, caput e § 3º (redação da Lei nº 14.532/2023)
Lei nº 7.716/1989, art. 2º-A (incluído pela Lei nº 14.532/2023)

readings.description: It is displaced: homotransphobic injúria is injúria racial under Lei 7.716 art. 2º-A, following the STF's extension of ADO 26 / MI 4733.

citations.cite: Lei 7.716/1989 art. 2º-A; Planalto heading '(Vide ADO Nº 26)'

STF, Plenário, MI 4733 ED (sessão virtual concluída em 21.8.2023), as reported by the TJRJ Portal do Conhecimento, 24.8.2023, reproducing the STF's news: "O Plenário do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) reconheceu que atos ofensivos praticados contra pessoas da comunidade LGBTQIAPN+ podem ser enquadrados como injúria racial."

readings.description: Art. 140 caput governs, because § 3º lists religion, age and disability only and art. 2º-A lists race, colour, ethnicity and national origin only.

citations.cite: CP art. 140 caput e § 3º; Lei 7.716/1989 art. 2º-A

readings.rejection_rationale: Struck by the STF in MI 4733 ED (2023): the interpretation that left offences against LGBTQIAPN+ persons outside injúria racial was the one the embargos corrected ("A interpretação que restringe sua aplicação aos casos de racismo e mantém desamparadas de proteção as ofensas racistas perpetradas contra indivíduos da comunidade LGBTQIAPN+ contraria não apenas o acórdão embargado, mas toda a sistemática constitucional", Min. Fachin, as reported).

taken.rationale: From 11.1.2023 (when art. 2º-A exists) an injúria for sexual orientation or gender identity, like one for race, colour, ethnicity or national origin (M-sweep-b-20), is not art. 140: `crime de injúria (art. 140)` is FALSE and `a injúria é a da Lei nº 7.716, de 1989, art. 2º-A` is TRUE. Before 11.1.2023 the earlier § 3º governed and is not encoded: the penalty refuses.

settled_by.citation: MI 4733 ED (Rel. Min. Edson Fachin), sessão virtual concluída em 21.8.2023; reported by the TJRJ Portal do Conhecimento, 24.8.2023 ("Fonte: STF")

readings.description: Concurrent: the victim may bring a queixa, or represent to the MP, which then brings a conditioned public action.
